questions.stem:
The table shows the number of female children born in the rural and urban areas of 4 different states (A to D) in 5 consecutive years (2020 to 2024).

| Year | A — Rural | A — Urban | B — Rural | B — Urban | C — Rural | C — Urban | D — Rural | D — Urban |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2020 | 700 | 925 | 495 | 825 | 905 | 910 | 1090 | 965 |
| 2021 | 825 | 1011 | 600 | 845 | 910 | 902 | 1230 | 1030 |
| 2022 | 910 | 1125 | 645 | 854 | 937 | 900 | 1160 | 1370 |
| 2023 | 1003 | 1210 | 765 | 950 | 1110 | 890 | 1340 | 1290 |
| 2024 | 1200 | 1315 | 630 | 980 | 1200 | 885 | 1250 | 1100 |

Which state recorded the highest number of female children born in the year 2024?
questions.explanation:
Add the rural and urban figures for 2024 in each state:

$$A: 1200 + 1315 = \mathbf{2515}$$
$$B: 630 + 980 = 1610$$
$$C: 1200 + 885 = 2085$$
$$D: 1250 + 1100 = 2350$$

The largest total is **State A** (2515).

*(Reading only the rural column would put A and C level at 1200 — the urban column is what separates them.)*

| Year | A — Rural | A — Urban | B — Rural | B — Urban | C — Rural | C — Urban | D — Rural | D — Urban |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2020 | 700 | 925 | 495 | 825 | 905 | 910 | 1090 | 965 |
| 2021 | 825 | 1011 | 600 | 845 | 910 | 902 | 1230 | 1030 |
| 2022 | 910 | 1125 | 645 | 854 | 937 | 900 | 1160 | 1370 |
| 2023 | 1003 | 1210 | 765 | 950 | 1110 | 890 | 1340 | 1290 |
| 2024 | 1200 | 1315 | 630 | 980 | 1200 | 885 | 1250 | 1100 |

In the year 2024, which state had the largest difference in the number of female children born between its rural and urban areas?
questions.explanation:
Take the 2024 row and subtract, ignoring sign:

$$A: |1200 - 1315| = 115$$
$$B: |630 - 980| = \mathbf{350}$$
$$C: |1200 - 885| = 315$$
$$D: |1250 - 1100| = 150$$

**State B** has the biggest gap, 350.

*(B has the smallest numbers overall, so the largest *difference* need not belong to the largest state — C is a close second at 315.)*

| Year | A — Rural | A — Urban | B — Rural | B — Urban | C — Rural | C — Urban | D — Rural | D — Urban |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2020 | 700 | 925 | 495 | 825 | 905 | 910 | 1090 | 965 |
| 2021 | 825 | 1011 | 600 | 845 | 910 | 902 | 1230 | 1030 |
| 2022 | 910 | 1125 | 645 | 854 | 937 | 900 | 1160 | 1370 |
| 2023 | 1003 | 1210 | 765 | 950 | 1110 | 890 | 1340 | 1290 |
| 2024 | 1200 | 1315 | 630 | 980 | 1200 | 885 | 1250 | 1100 |

What was the percentage increase in the female children born in state C from the year 2023 to 2024?
questions.explanation:
Total both areas of state C for each year:
$$2023: 1110 + 890 = 2000$$
$$2024: 1200 + 885 = 2085$$

$$\text{Increase} = 2085 - 2000 = 85.$$

$$\%\text{ increase} = \frac{85}{2000}\times 100 = \mathbf{4.25\%}.$$

*(The urban figure actually **fell** by 5; only the rural rise of 90 keeps the total growing.)*

Which is the only state which recorded a continuous fall in the number of female children born in its urban area over the last 5 consecutive years?
questions.explanation:
Read each state's **urban** column downwards and check that every step decreases:

$$A: 925 \to 1011 \to 1125 \to 1210 \to 1315 \;(\text{rising})$$
$$B: 825 \to 845 \to 854 \to 950 \to 980 \;(\text{rising})$$
$$C: 910 \to 902 \to 900 \to 890 \to 885 \;(\textbf{falling every year})$$
$$D: 965 \to 1030 \to 1370 \to 1290 \to 1100 \;(\text{up then down})$$

Only **State C** falls at every step.

questions.stem:
The line graph shows the profits of a company (in ₹ lakhs) over 4 years:

| Year | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Profit (₹ lakhs) | 80 | 100 | 120 | 150 |

What is the percentage increase in profit from 2019 to 2022?
questions.explanation:
The increase is measured **against the earlier year**:
$$150 - 80 = 70.$$

$$\%\text{ increase} = \frac{70}{80}\times 100 = 87.5\% \approx \mathbf{87\%}.$$

*(Dividing by 150 instead would give 46% — option 4 — which is the trap.)*

questions.stem:
The line graph shows the profits of a company (in ₹ lakhs) over 4 years:

| Year | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Profit (₹ lakhs) | 80 | 100 | 120 | 150 |

The percentage increase in profit during 2020 to 2021 is:
questions.explanation:
$$\frac{120 - 100}{100}\times 100 = \frac{20}{100}\times 100 = \mathbf{20\%}.$$

*(The jump is 20 lakhs on a base of 100 lakhs — the base year is 2020, not 2021.)*

questions.stem:
The line graph shows the profits of a company (in ₹ lakhs) over 4 years:

| Year | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Profit (₹ lakhs) | 80 | 100 | 120 | 150 |

For how many years was the profit of the company more than one crore rupees?
questions.explanation:
One crore $= 100$ lakhs, and the graph is drawn in ₹ lakhs. So the question asks how many years exceed **100**:

$$2019: 80 \;(\text{no}), \quad 2020: 100 \;(\text{equal, not more}),$$
$$2021: 120 \;(\textbf{yes}), \quad 2022: 150 \;(\textbf{yes}).$$

$$\Rightarrow \mathbf{2} \text{ years}.$$

*(2020 sits exactly on one crore, so it does not count as "more than".)*

questions.stem:
The pie chart shows the expenditure breakdown of a family:

| Head | Rent | Food | Education | Transport | Others |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Share | 25% | 35% | 15% | 10% | 15% |

If the total monthly expenditure is ₹48,000, what is the amount spent on Education?

The pie chart shows the expenditure breakdown of a family:

| Head | Rent | Food | Education | Transport | Others |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Share | 25% | 35% | 15% | 10% | 15% |

If the total monthly expenditure is ₹48,000, how much more expenditure was incurred on Rent compared to Education?
questions.explanation:
Work with the **difference in percentages** first — it saves a step:
$$25\% - 15\% = 10\%.$$

$$0.10 \times 48000 = \mathbf{₹4{,}800}.$$

*(Longer route: Rent $= ₹12{,}000$, Education $= ₹7{,}200$, difference $= ₹4{,}800$ ✓)*

questions.stem:
The pie chart shows the expenditure breakdown of a family:

| Head | Rent | Food | Education | Transport | Others |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Share | 25% | 35% | 15% | 10% | 15% |

If the expenditure on Transport is ₹8,000, what is the expenditure on Education and Rent put together for the same family?
questions.explanation:
**Step 1 — find the total.** Transport is 10% of it:
$$0.10 \times T = 8000 \Rightarrow T = ₹80{,}000.$$

**Step 2 — add the two shares:**
$$\text{Education } 15\% + \text{Rent } 25\% = 40\%.$$

$$0.40 \times 80000 = \mathbf{₹32{,}000}.$$

*(Note the total here is ₹80,000, not the ₹48,000 of the previous questions — each question sets its own base.)*
